candidates.title: Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
candidates.description:
This dataset contains locations of electric vehicle charging stations in Norfolk, VA as reported by the U.S. Department of Energy in their Alternative Fuels Data Center. 

Aligned with the City of Norfolk’s Climate Action Plan goal to increase energy efficiency, implement clean energy, and reduce vehicle reliance, electric vehicle charging stations will support the transition to a zero-emissions transportation sector. As electric vehicles become more common in Norfolk, this dataset will allow residents to locate charging stations based on type of charging port, access times, address, and other criteria. 

If you are aware of an electric vehicle charging port that is not listed, please submit a request via the Department of Energy’s Electric Vehicle Charging Station Locator to help us maintain the most accurate, up-to-date information for residents. 

This dataset will be updated daily.

candidates.title: Patent AT-E401657-T1: [Translated] ELECTRICAL SWITCHING DEVICE WITH REINFORCED ELECTRICAL CONTACTS
candidates.description: The switch has a mobile contactor element (30) connected to contact zones of fixed contactor elements (10, 20), where the elements are made of copper. The fixed contactor elements are in the form of coils and create an electromagnetic field (B) to form an attraction force (F) on the mobile element during passage of current. The fixed contactor elements are disposed opposite to each other, and the mobile contactor element is disposed between the coils to separate the contact zones of large height equal to the height of the coils.

candidates.title: Loudoun County Owned Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations
candidates.description:
This application displays the Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations that are operated and maintained by Loudoun County and available for public use.

The number of County operated and maintained Electric Vehicle Charging Stations continues to increase as the adopted FY 2023 Capital Improvement Program (CIP) budget provides funding for additional Electric Vehicle Charging Stations at County Facilities to be used by both County fleet and personal vehicles. This project consists of the planning, design, and construction of electric vehicle charging stations at existing County facilities.

The first phase of the project, underway with FY 2023 funds, prioritizes public-facing facilities such as parks, libraries, and community centers.

For more information about using EV chargers at metro parking garages in Loudoun County, see Metrorail Parking Garages in Loudoun County
